replies.text:
Here is a longer one about winter:

Snow settles on the fence posts one flake at a time,
each landing soundless, each one holding its place
until the yard forgets the shape of grass.

The kettle ticks. A window fogs and clears.
Somewhere a plough scrapes the road awake,
and the dog lifts one ear, then lets it fall.

By noon the light is thin as paper,
the kind you could read the sky through,
and the birds at the feeder take turns being brave.

Evening comes early and stays late.
We stack the wood, count the matches,
and let the dark be something we can sit beside.

Want me to turn one of these into a haiku as well?

Maple leaves let go,
the river carries their red —
morning fog lifts slow.

Want another one, or a different season?
I only have scripted answers in this demo.
